parsed.explanation: This division sits under an active national regime: nonmatching passports/visa screening, possible fraud/inadmissibility, federal facility restrictions, and documented immigration/corrections abuse including forced labour and sexual assault. These are traveler-facing universal-exposure measures, not merely resident law. Local law is comparatively protective—public-accommodation and hate-crime coverage, care shield for visiting patients, city/school all-gender access, X markers—but it cannot cancel national entry, document, facility, or custody rules. Litigation and some injunctions create uncertainty, not safety. The worst documented exposure is tier 1: federal document/facility mismatch and custody harm. Protective local machinery moves the division above a purely restrictive national average, but not above high risk. Thin enforcement data in this state is not evidence of safety because federal regimes apply; rating reflects what follows discovery.
